question: What is the attendance requirement to sit in the Major exam?
expected_answer: There is no attendance requirement to sit the Major exam. Circular 08-07-2024: "students' examination performance is no longer linked to their course attendance"; the student is still expected to have full attendance and "in any case, the attendance of a student should not fall below 75% in a course" (below 75% without a valid reason, the instructor can recommend de-registration from the course).
answer:
The attendance requirement to sit in the Major exam is that a student must have at least 75% attendance in the course. If a student's attendance falls below 75%, they are still allowed to appear for the exams but must score at least a C grade to pass the course. If they score below the cut-off for a C grade, they will be awarded an F grade.

Sources:
- Academic Regulations - students enrolled from July 2019 onwards, p.7 - https://iitj.ac.in/PageImages/Gallery/03-2025/1_Academic_Regulations_Final_03_09_2019.pdf

question: How many Open Elective credits do I need to earn in order to get a B.Tech. Degree?
expected_answer: Regulations (July 2019 onwards), Table 11.2: Open Electives (OE) = 10 for B.Tech. Regular (0 for B.Tech. with Specialization and Dual Degree). B.Tech. CSE curriculum (AY 2026 onwards): "Students in the regular B.Tech programme are required to complete 12 credits of open elective courses."
answer:
To earn a B.Tech. degree, a student must accumulate a minimum of **180 credits** in total. The distribution of these credits varies by program, but the **Open Elective** category is typically part of the elective credits. For example, in the B.Tech. (Computer Science & Engineering) program, students are required to earn **18 credits** from Open Electives. Similarly, in the B.Tech. (Electrical Engineering) program, the requirement is also **18 credits** for Open Electives. 

For other programs, such as B.Tech. (Mechanical Engineering) and B.Tech. (Biotechnology), the Open Elective credit requirement is also **18 credits**. However, for students pursuing a **B.Tech. with Minor** program, the Open Elective credit requirement is reduced to **zero**.

Circular 08-07-2024: "students' examination performance is no longer linked to their course attendance"; the student is still expected to have full attendance and "in any case, the attendance of a student should not fall below 75% in a course" (below 75% without a valid reason, the instructor can recommend de-registration from the course).
answer:
The attendance requirement to sit in the Major exam is that a student must have at least 75% attendance in the course. If a student's attendance falls below 75%, they will be allowed to appear for the exams but will need to score at least a C grade to pass the course. If their marks are lower than the cut-off for a C grade, they will be awarded an F grade.

question: What is the attendance requirement to sit in the Major exam?
expected_answer: There is no attendance requirement to sit the Major exam. answer:
The attendance requirement to sit in the Major exam is that a student's attendance should not fall below 75% in a course. This policy was amended in the Senate's 38th Meeting on 26th June 2024. Even if a student's attendance is below 75%, they are still allowed to appear for the exams, but they must score at least a C grade to pass the course. If they score below the cut-off for a C grade, they will be awarded an F grade.

question: What is the attendance requirement to sit in the Major exam?
expected_answer: There is no attendance requirement to sit the Major exam. Circular 08-07-2024: "students' examination performance is no longer linked to their course attendance"; the student is still expected to have full attendance and "in any case, the attendance of a student should not fall below 75% in a course" (below 75% without a valid reason, the instructor can recommend de-registration from the course).
answer:
The attendance requirement to sit in the Major exam is that a student's attendance should not fall below 75% in a course. This rule applies regardless of the student's performance in the exam. If a student's attendance falls below 75%, they will still be allowed to appear for the exams, but they will need to score at least a C grade to pass the course. If they score lower than the cut-off for a C grade, they will be awarded an F grade.

Sources:
